frequency_question: How often do major targeted reform bills backed by leadership intent successfully pass into law within a 26-month congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major structurally significant permitting, grid, or surface transportation reform packages (e.g., FAST Act 2015, Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act 2021). Excludes routine appropriations and minor technical corrections.

cases.name: FAST Act (Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act)

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 8 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.6x)
coverage_note: 5 major hits identified out of 8 comparable high-intent structural reform pushes in recent congressional history.
known_gaps: Excludes minor standalone provisions attached secretly to must-pass omnibus bills without standalone debate.
skeleton: Major bipartisan structural reform initiatives introduced with declared leadership intent across 15 two-year congressional terms since 1995.
multiplier: 5 successful major packages across approximately 8 major attempted structural reform cycles where principals signaled strong intent.
validity_reason: Valid through the duration of the current congressional structural and polarization dynamics, resetting at the start of the next 110th/111th equivalent session.
